title: A directed union of integer subalgebras is a categorical ring colimit
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and P a predicate on its Z-subalgebras. Assume the partial order I={A : Subalgebra Z R | P A} is nonempty and directed, and the supremum of its subalgebras is top. Let F:I to CommRing have object A and transition maps the inclusions, and let the inclusions into R define a cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then this cocone is colimiting. This is the already proved source theorem CommRingCat.isColimitSubalgebraCocone.

source.place: Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), third paragraph; details of the normalization and directed-union construction

proof.text: Use the partial order of integer subalgebras satisfying P as the index, with inclusions as transition maps and inclusions into R as a cocone. Nonempty directedness makes the category filtered by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

For any cocone, its ring maps from stages can be regarded as Z-algebra maps. Apply Mathlib Subalgebra.iSupLift to the directed family and the compatible algebra maps. The supremum-top hypothesis identifies the domain with R. The iSupLift_inclusion formula proves factorization through each stage.

For uniqueness, every x in R lies in a stage, by the directed-supremum union formula and supremum top. Two candidate ring maps agree on that stage, hence on x. This proves the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The adopted source declaration already implements this proof.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal P$ a property of subrings of $R$. Assume that the set $\mathcal I$ of subrings of $R$ having $\mathcal P$, partially ordered by inclusion, is nonempty and directed, and that these subrings generate $R$ (equivalently, as $\mathcal I$ is directed, $R=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal I}A$). Consider the diagram $\mathcal I\to(\text{commutative rings})$, $A\mapsto A$, whose transition maps are the inclusions, and the cocone on it with vertex $R$ given by the inclusions $A\hookrightarrow R$. Then this cocone is a colimit cocone in the category of commutative rings.

proof.text: The index category is the partially ordered set $\mathcal I$, which is nonempty and directed, hence a filtered category. Since $\mathcal I$ is directed, the subring generated by all $A\in\mathcal I$ is their union, so $R=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal I}A$.

Let $T$ be a commutative ring and $(\varphi_A:A\to T)_{A\in\mathcal I}$ ring maps compatible with the inclusions, i.e. $\varphi_{A'}|_A=\varphi_A$ for $A\subseteq A'$. Define $\varphi:R\to T$ by $\varphi(x)=\varphi_A(x)$ for any $A\in\mathcal I$ containing $x$. This is well defined: if $x\in A$ and $x\in A'$, choose $A''\in\mathcal I$ containing $A$ and $A'$; then $\varphi_A(x)=\varphi_{A''}(x)=\varphi_{A'}(x)$. It is a ring homomorphism: for $x,y\in R$ choose a single $A\in\mathcal I$ containing both (directedness), and use that $\varphi_A$ is a ring map; $\varphi(1)=\varphi_A(1)=1$. By construction $\varphi|_A=\varphi_A$ for every $A\in\mathcal I$, i.e. $\varphi$ factors the cocone.

For uniqueness, let $\varphi'$ be another ring map with $\varphi'|_A=\varphi_A$ for all $A$. Every $x\in R$ lies in some $A\in\mathcal I$, so $\varphi'(x)=\varphi_A(x)=\varphi(x)$. Hence the inclusion cocone with vertex $R$ satisfies the universal property of a colimit.
